svg.title: Why distributed compaction helps
svg.desc: Comparison of single-node compaction versus distributed compaction. On the left, a single compactor cannot keep up with the flush rate and writes stall under back-pressure. On the right, multiple workers consume the same submitted job queue in parallel. Note: L0 → L1 is shown for clarity; SlateDB actually uses size-tiered compaction where a single job can mix L0 SSTs with one or more sorted runs.
svg.text: Write path · flushes at high rate
immutable memtables pile up in RAM
capped by one node's CPU + network
the whole system: reads slow first,
Write path · flushes at high rate
drained as fast as it fills
Note: SlateDB uses size-tiered compaction. A single job spec can mix L0 SSTs
with one or more sorted runs (e.g. [L0:1, L0:2, SR:1] → SR:new). No explicit L1/L2.
